primary_citation.popular_name: SLAPPback — Malicious Prosecution After Anti-SLAPP Dismissal

key_holding: A SLAPPback is a malicious prosecution or abuse of process claim arising from a prior case dismissed via anti-SLAPP motion. SLAPPbacks get different treatment than ordinary malicious prosecution: (1) the filing window is 120 days (not 60), (2) discovery is NOT automatically stayed, (3) fees are NOT automatically awarded to the prevailing defendant, (4) a party who filed an illegal SLAPP cannot use anti-SLAPP against the SLAPPback. This section completes the anti-SLAPP ecosystem: §425.16 is the shield, §425.18 is the sword against those who weaponize litigation.

amendment_history.event: Stats. 2005, Ch. 535, Sec. 2. Added to provide remedy for malicious use of SLAPP litigation.
